record.paper_title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II: Overview and Open Problems
record.original_question: For DTCS(n), let N_n(j) be the number of clades of size j and define SS_n(α)=Σ_{j=2}^n N_n(j) j^α. Give a detailed analysis of SS_n(α), including its asymptotic behavior as a function of the real or complex parameter α.

evidence.quote: the sum of p-powers of subtree sizes. Our work provides some results and conjectures for that quantity SS(p)_n in our model, that is SS(p)_n := Xn_j=2 Nn(j)j^p

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define the discrete-time critical beta-splitting tree DTCS(n) as follows. Start with the root labeled by the integer n. Given any node labeled by an integer m ≥ 2, split it into two children with labels (L, m−L), where L ∈ {1, 2, …, m−1} is drawn from the distribution
  q(m, L) = (1/h_{m−1}) · (1/L + 1/(m−L)) / 2,  with h_{m−1} = Σ_{k=1}^{m−1} 1/k,
independently across nodes. Nodes labeled 1 are leaves and are not split further. The resulting random binary tree has exactly n leaves. A "clade" is the subtree rooted at any internal or leaf node; its "size" is the label at its root, equivalently the number of leaves it contains.

For each j ∈ {2, 3, …, n}, let N_n(j) denote the (random) number of clades of size j in DTCS(n). For a real or complex parameter α, define the random additive functional
  SS_n(α) := Σ_{j=2}^{n} N_n(j) · j^α.

Provide a detailed analysis of SS_n(α). In particular, determine, as functions of α ∈ ℂ:
(a) the asymptotic behavior of the mean E[SS_n(α)] as n → ∞;
(b) the asymptotic order and the asymptotic distribution of SS_n(α) (suitably centered and normalized);
(c) the location and nature of any phase transitions in α governing the limit regime.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in the overview paper on the critical beta-splitting tree. Recent follow-up work (2024–2025) on the critical beta-splitting model has resolved various central limit theorems for related functionals (leaf height, depth, fringe-tree structure) and developed Mellin-analysis and harmonic-descent-chain techniques, but no source found provides a complete detailed analysis of SS_n(α) as a function of complex α with full asymptotic distribution and phase transitions. The analogous question for conditioned Galton–Watson trees has been treated by Fill and Janson, but the beta-splitting case appears still open.

status_evidence.title: The sum of powers of subtree sizes for conditioned Galton-Watson trees
status_evidence.snippet: Limiting distribution transitions between complex-normal for Re(α)<0 and non-normal for Re(α)>0.
status_evidence.claim: Analogous problem solved for conditioned Galton-Watson trees, but not for beta-splitting model.

status_evidence.title: Some central limit theorems for critical beta-splitting trees
status_evidence.snippet: CLTs for various statistics of the critical beta-splitting random tree.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress on related functionals; SS_n(α) analysis not completed.
